steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: There is one thing I must reiterate, my dear.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: If you are only here to return the book, and are still unwilling to consider my prior suggestion, then leave it by the fireplace, and off you go.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Do you really mean that if I don't agree with your method, you won't even say another word to me?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Were this any other time, I would be happy to entertain your adorable follies of youth and talk with you into the wee hours of the night.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: I have missed much, after all. About you, your parents, and what you experienced in Chernobog...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I can just as well tell you all of this now.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: But I am in no position to listen.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Even when faced with a choice between life or death, I was unable to persuade you to accept my arrangements: to leave Grypherburg and lie low, or at least submit a testimony that brings you only benefit.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: I could not protect you, which leaves me ashamed to face your parents. How could I have the right to learn anything about them from you?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: It's not like that, Countess—

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Have you read the book?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I have, cover to cover. I now understand why you lent it to me.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: What does it say on the title page?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: 'There is no cause worth sacrificing a beautiful life.'

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Indeed, indeed. Yakov Petrov's Confessions, published posthumously by his family. A discussion about a traitor's experiences, bought with his life. So, I simply do not understand...

spans.text: , published posthumously by his family. A discussion about a traitor's experiences, bought with his life. So, I simply do not understand...

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: If you already know that people have paid the ultimate price for these experiences, and you still have the freedom to choose another path, then why must you repeat the mistakes of the past?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Surely you do not have to be on your deathbed, perhaps even choking on blood in prison like he did, to know what you believe in is doomed to be a flash in the pan, forgotten by history?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Countess, I...

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Tell me, child. Tell me why.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: ...To be honest, I have asked myself the same question. But if...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Forgive my shamelessness, but I have a request of you.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: If I write my testimony as you say and save myself, can you promise me that the other members of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group will be treated equally as well?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Of course! So long as you do as those people want, and list out some specific names in your testimony—

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Very well. I will do as you say.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I will submit a testimony like this one to the hearing...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: A 'confession'.

steps.name: Impatient Noble
steps.text: Countess?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Ah, yes, I'm listening. What did you say?

steps.name: Impatient Noble
steps.text: Pardon me. I simply wished to notify you that the arbiter has just mentioned Baryshnya Rostova. He will require you to hand over her testimony in a moment.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Our next witness is Baryshnya Natalya Rostova. Due to special circumstances, she is unable to attend in person today.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: However, she has requested that her testimony be read by someone else, on her behalf.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Your Honor—

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Baryshnya Rostova sent me a letter yesterday. I'd like to request the committee to look over said letter, and permit me to read it aloud.
As the parliamentarian accepts the letter in Absinthe's hand, the whispers in the gallery grow and grow. Countess Vorontsova senses countless gazes upon her. She shakes her head.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Very well. The hearing asks Young Zoya to recite what knowledge Baryshnya Rostova offers about this incident on her behalf.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: 'To the honorable and esteemed ladies and gentlemen of the committee, this is a confession...'

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: 'Due to my remorse, and the sensitive nature of the contents of this letter, I will not mention the specific names of any nobles, save for Pavlovich, who must be discussed.'

steps.name: Impatient Noble
steps.text: (Quietly) Countess, what we said was to—

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Hear her out.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: '...I hope this will be sufficient to win your trust.'

a.text: 'Not long after the incident at the ball, due to a deep worry over Sonya's safety, I begged a person of influence for aid, successfully contacting the parents of most of the students who were arrested that day.'

spans.text: 'Not long after the incident at the ball, due to a deep worry over Sonya's safety, I begged a person of influence for aid, successfully contacting the parents of most of the students who were arrested that day.'

a.text: 'I then learned that all the 'criminals' who trespassed on Tsarevgrad had been locked away in Katorga, the place the people now call the 'quarantine zone'.'

spans.text: 'I then learned that all the 'criminals' who trespassed on Tsarevgrad had been locked away in Katorga, the place the people now call the 'quarantine zone'.'

a.text: 'What surprised me was that, despite there being no small number of illustrious lords and ladies among the parents, they too found it difficult to obtain concrete information on the goings-on in the quarantine zone.'

spans.text: 'What surprised me was that, despite there being no small number of illustrious lords and ladies among the parents, they too found it difficult to obtain concrete information on the goings-on in the quarantine zone.'

a.text: 'Included among them are some who consider themselves of sensitive identity, which rendered it inappropriate for them to visit Katorga. And so, they entrusted me to be the parents' delegate, and bade me visit the arrested students.'

spans.text: 'Included among them are some who consider themselves of sensitive identity, which rendered it inappropriate for them to visit Katorga. And so, they entrusted me to be the parents' delegate, and bade me visit the arrested students.'

a.text: 'They recommended I call upon the administrator of Katorga, one Magistrate Pavlovich. To visit him, I climbed the wall that divided the zone from the rest of Terra the following day.'

spans.text: 'They recommended I call upon the administrator of Katorga, one Magistrate Pavlovich. To visit him, I climbed the wall that divided the zone from the rest of Terra the following day.'

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: ...Haha, I met with a friend of your father's, Baron Shuvalov. He borrowed heavily, then ran off to Chernobog to invest it all, only to return to Grypherburg with absolutely nothing to his name.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: But when I met him the day before yesterday, his hands were shackled, and he was being escorted by two police officers out of the city, to be sent east. My curiosity had me asking him what great crime he had committed to be sentenced to exile.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: He had quite the air of mystery as he whispered in my ear that during a banquet, he shouted: 'Long live the miners'.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: I was absolutely flabbergasted, so I asked him why. Can you guess what he said?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Forgive me, but nothing comes to mind.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: He laughed as he turned to look at the officers with him, saying: 'If I'm exiled, my creditors can't find me, hahahaha.'

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: What a... unique anecdote. If I didn't have more pressing matters at hand, I would be happy to listen to them all day.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Oh, look at me, such a windbag. Most deserving of your mockery.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Come, my dear Baryshnya Rostova. Let's talk business.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: My good magistrate, I am here for—
The shrill whine of a power drill interrupts the conversation. Pavlovich gives Rosa an apologetic wave of the hand before walking to the door.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: What's going on? Who's in charge today? Send them to me this instant!

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Ruffian
steps.text: Thousand pardons, sir, we brought in quite a few people last night—

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: What do I care how many people you have? Don't you know I'm entertaining a guest right now?

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Ruffian
steps.text: I'll have them stop right away.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Terribly sorry about that. What were you going to say?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Pardon my curiosity, but...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Each raion of Deity Grypherburg has its own guard unit, but they are given standardized equipment. I noticed the man you spoke to just now held a weapon, but was wearing plainclothes. Is there something special about Katorga?

spans.text: of Deity Grypherburg has its own guard unit, but they are given standardized equipment. I noticed the man you spoke to just now held a weapon, but was wearing plainclothes. Is there something special about Katorga?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Special? Haha, you jest, Baryshnya Rostova, unless you believe a garbage dump to be special.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Ever since Grypherburg's factories received an upgrade, the old industrial zones lay idle. Some councilors suggested they could be refurbished and put to other uses.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Like, for example, having a place to lock up criminals and the poor folk who refuse to move, while also performing some light manufacturing. Two fowls with one stone.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Things started off rather well. If it were not for the shortage of resources these past few months, these factories would not have all shut down.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: *Sigh* Ursus has never been one to pay useless places any heed. Proper guards are limited in manpower, and what funds have been given to me are only enough to hire idiots to help manage things.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: It's a miracle that these fools haven't caused an accident yet.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: That drill earlier did not sound like it was for putting up renovations—

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Ah, my humblest apologies if it startled you. Just the dentist at work. I rather wish he would not disturb my guests.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: A dentist? Here?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Yes, they drill away cavities, after all. They scrape away the rot, and fill the hole with new materials... No matter if they work with enamel, or thoughts.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Now, I believe your curiosity has been sated. Shall we return to business?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: ...My apologies for taking us off-track.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: You saw my list of names when I first arrived. Their parents have entrusted me to check on their well-being. I hope you can tell me how they are doing.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Especially considering that among these names, there are many heirs of great and powerful nobles. I hope you can be accommodating.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Naturally, naturally. It appears this batch of arrestees really are all students. Oh, pity the hearts of parents everywhere. I know just how worried people of such renown must be about their heirs.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: If these children had the least bit of empathy for their parents, why would they display such disgraceful, heartbreaking behavior?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: But you must understand just how concerned I am for the future of Katorga.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Before we proceed to the next step of our discussions, I must reiterate that the parents who have entrusted me with this task wish to confirm the condition of their children.

spans.text: Before we proceed to the next step of our discussions, I
reiterate that the parents who have entrusted me with this task wish to confirm the condition of their children.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Yes, yes, there'll be plenty of time for you to see how they're doing in a moment.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: There happen to be two names on this list that I would like to discuss further with you, Baryshnya Rostova.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: By all means.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: The first is Naum. As far as I'm aware, he was released yesterday. Most likely already arrived home as you were making your way here.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Thank you for informing me. I shall check with his parents as soon as possible.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Ahem. Next is this girl, Sonya.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: She's managed to make quite the name for herself these past few days. I heard about many things involving her from my underlings.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: How is she?
Natalya gets the sudden sensation that something has changed in the ever-present smile plastered on Pavlovich's face.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: No need to be so tense. I am simply curious myself. She is no noble, nor the daughter of a rich household. Just an ordinary student. So why exactly is she on the list of names?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I had no intention of hiding it from you. It is simple: Sonya is one of my friends, and she is no black-hearted thug, which is why I added her to the list. I beg you, let me check on her.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: O, bozhe moi. When the scion of the House of Rostov asks me for aid, how could I ever refuse?

spans.text: . When the scion of the House of Rostov asks me for aid, how could I ever refuse?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: However, you must agree to two things: first, talk to Sonya and get her to sit still without fidgeting about for a few days. I guarantee that she'll be out of the quarantine zone in several days' time.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Secondly, go to the parents you represent, have them pressure the State Council into repealing their proposal and retaining the quarantine zone, by all means available.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: 'Retaining' the quarantine zone? Do you mean the quarantine will soon be revoked?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Oh my, did our dear Countess Vorontsova not tell you? This is no simple revocation, but rather... pure renunciation.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: The exhaustion of the empire's resources is no secret. Ursus is desperate enough to abandon one of the capital's industrial plates, all for the sake of economization.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: A week ago, the State Council proposed to cast off the quarantine zone, leaving it to the wilds. This proposal was permitted to move forward by the Chairman, which means His Imperial Majesty must tacitly approve of it.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Fortunately, with the help of some old nobles who support me, this plan has been delayed. But we cannot stave it off forever.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: I noticed many renowned industrial nobles on your list. If those nobles can drum up support from their friends and stand as a united front in opposition, I'm sure His Imperial Majesty and the State Council will reconsider.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: This is all for the sake of their children's lives. They would not dare be lax. If I receive an edict saying the quarantine zone shall be retained, then I release everyone.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: ...Do you believe I can do this?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: I have hope, at the very least. With only a list of names in hand, you fearlessly strode into this place that all other souls shun, even seeking to save your friend.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: And so, everyone's lives are in your hands, Baryshnya Natalya Rostova. Including Sonya's.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I will pass on your requests. But first, I must see her.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Naturally.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Come, Khvoin.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Take this young lady to Sonya. And remember to announce her as Natalya.

steps.name: Hired Muscle
steps.text: We're not far from that sterva—I mean, Sonya's camp. You wait here, I'll go give her a heads-up.

spans.text: —I mean, Sonya's camp. You wait here, I'll go give her a heads-up.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: She's already set up a camp here? And do you really need to give her a 'heads-up'?

steps.name: Hired Muscle
steps.text: You're her friend, which means you know you don't mess with her.
The corners of Rosa's mouth curl up into a subtle smile, unbidden. As a gust of wind blows over from the depths of the gloomy street, she turns her head, holding onto her hat.

Suddenly, a gray shadow jumps out of some ruins. Merely a skinny cloudbeast, its skin mange-marked. It stops in the middle of the road, vigilantly watching Rosa as it clamps down on something between its teeth.
Rosa's pupils contract. It is a human finger, pale, stiff, black mud and dried blood staining its cracked nail, the fractured end like a chewed-up branch.

steps.name: Hired Muscle
steps.text: Blyat! Stupid beast!

steps.name: Hired Muscle
steps.text: Are you alright, Natalya?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I... Nothing, it just... No, it's nothing.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: It's terribly cold out here. I must trouble you to ask Sonya to come out as quickly as possible.

steps.name: Hired Muscle
steps.text: Right away.
As she watches the man fade from view, a wave of cold seeps down from Rosa's head to her toes. Under its assault, her upright bearing slackens.
She staggers, leaning against a frigid brick wall as she covers her mouth. She forces the bile back down her throat, but she cannot stop the tears streaming from her eyes.
A finger. A shriek from some poor, humiliated soul. A turbid memory of Chernobog. They all flail wildly through her mind.
This is not her first time experiencing this. She can face this alone—
No, you cannot be like this, Natalya. This is unseemly, impermissible, surmountable.
Rosa huddles on the ground, the metallic taste of cold air invading her mouth as she takes deep breaths, trying to stop her arms from shaking—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Natalya?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: (Ragged breathing)

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You're hyperventilating—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Chyort! Can you hear me, Natalya?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I-I—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Where are you right now?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I'm... I'm... in the quarantine zone...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Yeah, the quarantine zone—Blyat! Why do you all keep coming here one after another? You want to die or something?

spans.text: Why do you all keep coming here one after another? You want to die or something?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Now's not the time for that talk. Listen to me, Natalya. I'm here with you. You are not alone.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Natalya!

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Sonya...?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Yeah, it's me. You okay?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Sonya... No, I'm fine. I'm so happy to see you...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: And to see that you're fine too.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You're still babbling. How many fingers?
Zima extends three of her fingers, shoving them into Rosa's face.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Three.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Phew. Your brain's in one piece, at least.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I'm fine, really. It was just the wind making me cough, and my heart felt a little uncomfortable because of that. I'm feeling much better now, thank you.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Enough, don't put on an act when you're with me. Did the guy who was looking for me cause you trouble?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I'm really not... *sigh* Forget it.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Listen, Sonya, I can only be here for a short time, so I must catch you up on everything as quickly as possible.
Rosa looks around, hinting to Zima that she should lean in closer.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I know you were sent by the guy in charge.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Let me tell you something first, Leto's already here. Anything else you need to know from me?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Rosalind... She's been insisting on finding you. She left only a note at the branch office before running off.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Don't be too hard on her, she just wanted to come and help me ASAP... I-I wanted to ask, how's everyone doing?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Is Gummy okay? Is Istina mad at me? And Zoya and Instructor Dur-nar...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Everyone's fine, but they're all worried about you.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I myself came to make sure you're safe, as well as this quarantine zone...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I don't know what you've seen so far, but the stuff that's happened here is probably way worse than that.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: No food, no fuel, not even clean water. People are forming gangs and fighting everywhere over territory and resources.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Every day, people die.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Pavlovich said he will release everyone, as long as some conditions are met—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Do you really trust a guy like that?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Of course not...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I know there's nothing else you could do. Otherwise you wouldn't have had to ask all over the place for help getting in, just to see how I was doing and tell me the news.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Gotta say, even though everything I said earlier felt scary as hell, and it feels like everyone might just die tomorrow, it's nothing we haven't seen before.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: A locked-off city that nobody cares about, even if it explodes, a group of students almost running on instinct, crushing each other to survive...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: It's got a familiar ring to it, doesn't it?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Tell me, what do you need right now? I can leave this place, and once I meet up with everyone outside, we'll think of a way—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I need to know how many people are on those fortress-like raion walls. Excluding the thugs.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Not very many. Pavlovich has a few bodyguards. Shouldn't be more than ten, if we include those wearing old army uniforms.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Not too bad.
Zima leans even closer to Rosa, lowering her voice as low as it will go.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: (Whispers) If you can, come up with a laundry list of ideas to cut off their supply of weapons.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: (Whispers) Weapons? But the 'security' I saw were hardly professionals.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: (Whispers) There's a lot you don't know.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: (Whispers) They've been bringing in ammo and heavy weapons every day for the past few days. If every guard on the walls has that kind of firepower, we don't stand a chance.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: You mean...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I mean exactly what I said.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: ...I see. Once we get out, I will talk to the others, and we will figure something out.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Sonya, you and Rosalind need to take care of yourselves. You must.

spans.text: Sonya, you and Rosalind need to take care of yourselves. You

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Don't worry. I'll get out of here, and I'm bringing everybody with me.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Just like before.
